title: Department of Veterans Affairs: Phase 56H Evidence Decision
publisher: Department of Veterans Affairs Office of Inspector General
summary: VA OIG found insufficient iFAMS access limitation for all 20 Technology Acquisition Center users sampled; 91 percent of 2,818 users with TAC-data access did not work for TAC, and 78 percent held roles granting exceptionally broad access. Phase 56H decision: The named-system control layer deepens materially, but the selected evidence state remains Partially Closed because the new recommendations are open and the FY 2025 FISMA result remains missing.
key_findings: Highest-value missing record: FY 2025 FISMA result plus named-system control operation.
Evidence state: Partially Closed to Partially Closed.
Continuation rule: Reopen when VA OIG publishes the FY 2025 FISMA audit or closes the named iFAMS recommendations.
why_it_matters: The record tests a named acquisition or reopening rule while keeping adjacent context separate from exact operating, corrective-action, or closure evidence.
ftfn_relevance: Records the official rail, compatible observation, and decision at a date.
Separates evidence-state movement from entity performance, quality, readiness, or value.
evidence_limits: The sample and access-role findings apply to the named system and observation period; they are not a department-wide incident or service-outcome denominator.
Recommendation closure, corrected access-state testing, FY 2025 FISMA results, incidents, recovery, service effects, and veteran outcomes.
No causal effect, ranking, composite score, readiness score, or unsupported cross-entity comparison is supported.
